title: Things to Do in Mexico City: Three Stops for a More Playful Visit
description: Explore Alameda Central, the Palacio Postal exterior and Palacio de Minería on a focused Mexico City outing through the Centro Histórico.
body:
For things to do in Mexico City that fit into a focused outing, start in the Centro Histórico. Alameda Central, the Palacio Postal exterior and Palacio de Minería offer a park and two very different buildings within a manageable part of the centre.

This plan concentrates on public paths and exterior views. You can enjoy it without making museum admission or an interior tour part of the day.

1. Begin with a pause in Alameda Central

Alameda Central is a historic public park with promenades, planting and fountains. The city tourism guide describes its long history and place in the life of the centre.

Choose an open path and take some time before heading toward the larger buildings nearby. A park can be a place to orient yourself as well as somewhere to rest. You do not need to find every fountain or wait for an empty bench to enjoy being there.

Plan the stop: Use public paths and current open entrances. Stay out of planting beds and fountain basins. Events or maintenance can change access, so build the visit around what is open rather than a particular feature being available.

2. Look at the Palacio Postal from Tacuba

The Palacio Postal stands at Calle de Tacuba and Eje Central. Its elaborate exterior gives a working civic building an unusually decorative presence. The official tourism guide to the Postal Palace explains the building’s postal purpose and architecture.

Enjoy the façade from a safe public pavement position. There is enough to appreciate outside without committing to the building’s interior. This is a useful stop for noticing how much attention can be given to a place associated with an everyday service.

Plan the stop: Use designated crossings at Eje Central and Tacuba and leave room for people entering the building. Mailing something, buying stamps and entering the post office are not required. Interior access follows separate current arrangements.

3. Continue to Palacio de Minería

A little farther along Tacuba, Palacio de Minería faces the Plaza Manuel Tolsá area. The city’s building guide explains its connection to mining education and the work of architect Manuel Tolsá.

From the public pavement, the façade offers a different architectural impression from the Postal Palace. Give yourself time with that contrast without turning it into a test. The value of seeing the two buildings near one another is that each can make you more attentive to the other.

Plan the stop: This suggestion stays outside. Museum, library and event access are separate, and an open main entrance does not mean every interior area is available to visitors.

Keep the Centro Histórico outing focused

Begin in Alameda Central, use open public routes and designated crossings to reach the Postal Palace, then continue east along Tacuba to Palacio de Minería. Allow roughly two to three hours including pauses.

The three suggested public-space visits need no attraction tickets. Transport, food and optional interior visits are separate. Use a current map for the connection around the Bellas Artes area, and allow time at busy crossings. If your day already includes a long museum visit, the two building exteriors can make a smaller outing on their own.
